newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - AUSTRALIA 10-YR BOND ATTEMPTING REBOUND.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - AUSTRALIA 10-YR BOND ATTEMPTING REBOUND.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract put in a modest bounce during SYCOM trade after the rapid slide in prices seen either side of the weekend.
*Bond needs to secure break of 93.310 for firmer footing.
The September Australian 10-year bond futures contract put in a modest bounce during SYCOM trade after the rapid slide in prices seen either side of the weekend.
The contract ended after-hours trade at 93.260, up from Monday's pit close of 93.195 and intra day low of 93.165.

Monday's test of a 4-1/2 month rising trendline at the intra day low has proved to be the base for the partial recovery, but technical analysts believe the contract needs to secure a break back above 93.310 to put the market on a firmer footing.
However, sentiment has been severely jarred as the correction from an August 1 record of 93.695 gathered pace.
U.S. Treasuries, which have been the driving force for the local market's sell-off, ended Monday's session narrowly mixed.

The U.S. is expected remain nervous in the run up to Wednesday's retail sales data, although comments by Fed Reserve governor Susan Phillips hinting that there was no immediate need for a tightening went some way to soothe the market.

Locally, the key focus will be on a speech by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane in Perth later on Tuesday (11.00 p.m./1300 GMT), his first public appearence since last month's official rate cut to 5.0 percent.
